notes.decision: Translated 'the Call' per accumulated vocabulary entry ⲡⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲡⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ (Manichaean Call/Hearing pair). Here paired in the title with the descent into the soul's members.
Translated 'how many' — Lycopolitan interrogative reflex of Sahidic ⲟⲩⲏⲣ. Confirmed by parallel 'ⲍⲛ̄ ⲉϣ ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ' in line 10 = 'into how many members.'
Translated 'he was spread forth' — same root as glossary's ⲥⲁⲣϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'spread forth, scatter forth' with 3sg.m suffix. Variant spelling without ϩ.

Translated literally as 'a house of wood.' ϣⲉ in Lycopolitan = Sahidic ϣⲉ 'wood.' The image fits Manichaean cosmology where the cosmic body is structured like a built dwelling. Could alternatively imply 'wooden house/tree-house' as image for the multi-membered cosmic body.

Translated 'he was released forth' — ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'release' (glossary) with 3sg.m suffix; could be reflexive 'released himself.' Subject ambiguous; rendered as passive in keeping with the cosmological scene of the First Man's emanation.

Translated 'being attached therein' — ⲁϥⲧ qualitative of ⲁϣⲧ̄/ⲱϣⲧ̄ 'hang, be suspended' + ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧⲥ 'in her' (referring to the head/ⲁⲡⲉ feminine in Coptic). Members of the soul hang from/attach to the head as their root.
Translated 'upon' — Lycopolitan reflex of ⲉϫⲙ̄/ϩⲓϫⲙ̄ 'upon, on top of.' Standard cosmological prepositional usage.
Translated 'established' — qualitative of ⲧⲁϫⲣⲟ 'establish, make firm' (Lycopolitan ⲭ for ϫ). Standard verb of cosmic stabilization.
Translated 'which he wears' — ⲣ̄- + φορεῖ (cf. accumulated vocab ⲣ̄ⲫⲟⲣⲥ 'bear/wear') + ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲥ 3sg.f. object. The Father wears the Virgin (= Soul) as his garment.
Treated the overlined ⲉ̄ at line start as a section/marginal numeral (5) preserved within the body; left as parenthetical '(5)' in English. Could alternatively be a textual marker.
Greek-derived participle from χαλάω 'loosen, slack'; rendered 'slackened.' Could alternatively be a corruption. Confidence low.

Plural noun of unclear etymology. Tentatively rendered 'bewildered ones' from context (those among whom the slackened soul exists). Could relate to ⲡⲱⲱϩⲥ̄ 'distress' or be a Greek loan. Flag for parallels.

Translated 'beautiful fragrance.' Lyc. ϣⲙ̄ⲛⲟⲩϩⲉ likely orthographic variant of ϣⲙⲛⲟⲩϥⲉ 'fragrance, incense' (Sah. with ϥ; Lyc. with ϩ via dialectal alternation). Fits the liturgical greeting series: peace + kiss + fragrance.

Greek πύργος 'tower' with diminutive πυργίσκος, or with adjectival/extended ending. Translated 'the tower' / 'the towered one'; cosmological referent (likely the cosmic tower or watchtower of the soul-gathering apparatus).

Parsed as ⲁ-ⲡ-ⲟⲩⲱⲍⲙⲉ 'to the answering' — Lyc. ⲟⲩⲱⲍⲙⲉ = nominalization of ⲟⲩⲱϣⲃ 'answer, respond' (cf. ⲡⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ 'the Answer' in vocab). The faculties stand at their place 'for the answering' in the icon of the Father — the cosmic call/answer pattern.

Relative perfect 'who found him' — masculine object suffix ϩ (Lyc. for ϥ). Subject from prior context (likely the Father or one of the apostolic emissaries finding the soul-emissary in the Virgin of Light).
